entry.title: Kubernetes Admission Control: From Pod Security Standards to Policy-as-Code Gates
entry.summary:
Kubernetes Admission Control: From Pod Security Standards to Policy-as-Code Gates
Kubernetes security guidance often stops at recommendations. Admission control is where recommendations become gates that a workload cannot pass without meeting them. A cluster that relies on documentation and review will eventually run a workload that violates its own rules. Admission controllers evaluate requests before objects are persisted, which means a policy can reject a non-compliant pod rather than relying on someone noticing it later. The built-in Pod Security Standards provide a baseline without any additional tooling. Policy engines extend that baseline to organization-specific rules.
